headers.//: Vite fingerprints the bundle, so these filenames change whenever their contents do. A year of immutable caching is safe precisely because a new build produces a new name. Matched by extension rather than by folder: dist/assets also holds the unhashed copies of public/assets, and caching og-banner.png for a year would mean a redesigned banner staying stale in every social crawler until 2027.

Everything served straight out of public/ keeps its name across deploys, so it gets a day. Long enough to be worth caching, short enough that replacing an icon or the banner takes effect the same afternoon.
index.html must never be cached hard: it is what points at the current hashed bundle, so a stale copy pins a visitor to an old build.
nosniff stops a browser second-guessing a declared content type. SAMEORIGIN stops the site being framed by someone else's page.
